title: Filename filter UX is confusing as it's not clear setting mimetypes is also required
line: The desktop's "Hide matching"/"Show matching" file name filter now works out of the box, and the Filter page says when no file type is checked.
explanation: A file only matches the Folder View filter when its name fits the pattern and its type is in the checked list. The default list is the "all/all" wildcard, but the Filter page showed it as every type unchecked, and applying the page then saved an empty list, so a pattern like *.png matched nothing and the filter silently did nothing (or hid everything with "Show matching"). The page now shows the wildcard as every type checked and saves every type checked back as "all/all" (so types added later still match), and an inline message explains that the pattern only applies to checked types whenever none is checked.

commits.message:
containments/desktop: make the Filter page's file type rule visible

The default "all/all" file types showed as unchecked and applying saved
an empty list, so the name pattern never matched. Show them as checked,
save every type checked as "all/all" and say when none is checked.

BUG: 502692

media.caption: Master: Hide matching, *.png, default file types (shown unchecked), applied: a.png is still on the desktop.
Fixed: the default file types show as checked; Hide matching *.png hides a.png, b.txt stays, and the types are saved as all/all.
Master: a pattern with no file type checked, and nothing on the page says types are needed.
Fixed: after Deselect All, the page explains that the pattern only applies to checked types.

review.text: This fixes the real root cause cleanly in MimeTypesModel and ConfigFilter.qml: the default "all/all" (and legacy "all/allfiles") wildcard now shows every file type checked and round-trips back to "all/all" when all rows are checked, so filename filters work out of the box without silently saving an empty type list. Switching the delegate CheckBox to bind directly to the model's checked role fixes checkbox state tracking, and the Kirigami.InlineMessage clearly explains the rule whenever no types are checked. Before/after screenshots and regression checks thoroughly confirm the behavior.
